tasks.title: approve command: founder approvals of a lead, draft, audience or offer with a written-approval reference
tasks.goal: Record each founder approval with approver, approval date, scope, the item approved and a reference to the founder's written approval as an append-only approval activity, refusing without the reference; a draft approval names its lead and the draft's SHA-256 (R-18).
tasks.plan:
1. cottonwood/gate.py: GateError(field, message) with str 'FIELD: MESSAGE'; SCOPES ('lead','draft','claim','audience','offer'); Approval frozen dataclass (activity_id, scope, item, approver, lead_id, approved_on) with line(); approve(conn, scope, item, approver, reference, day, lead_id, actor, now) that strips and checks approver/reference/actor, resolves the item per scope (lead: integer id that exists; draft: --lead required and existing, the path must be an existing file, sha256 of its bytes; audience/offer: non-blank text, optional existing --lead), and appends one 'approval' activity with events._insert_activity in a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (occurred_at events._day_start(day), recorded_at now). The 'claim' scope raises GateError('scope', 'claim approvals arrive with the claims file') until T-02.
2. cottonwood/cli.py: approve Command: positional scope (choices SCOPES) and item, --approver (required), --reference (required argparse-wise but blank refused by gate), --lead int, --date (events._parse_entry_date, default events.denver_today(); bad -> 'error: date: ...'), --actor, --db; refusals 'error: FIELD: MESSAGE' exit 1.
3. tests/test_approve.py with utc_now pinned to 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z: printed lines, stored payloads (sha256 computed in the test with hashlib), audience/offer with and without --lead, every refusal with no activity appended, unknown scope exit 2.
acceptance_criteria: With utc_now pinned to 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z and lead 1 stored, 'cottonwood approve lead 1 --approver Founder --reference "email 2026-11-29 Re: first prospects"' exits 0, prints 'approval 1 recorded: lead 1 by Founder', and appends one 'approval' activity with lead_id 1 whose payload has scope 'lead', item '1', approver 'Founder', reference 'email 2026-11-29 Re: first prospects' and approved_on '2026-11-30'; the same command with '--date 2026-11-29' records approved_on '2026-11-29'.

'cottonwood approve draft DRAFT --lead 1 --approver Founder --reference "email 2026-11-30 Re: draft 1"' for an existing file DRAFT exits 0, prints 'approval N recorded: draft DRAFT for lead 1 by Founder' (N the activity id), and stores scope 'draft', item equal to the DRAFT argument, lead_id 1 and a payload 'sha256' equal to hashlib.sha256 of the file's bytes as hex.

'approve audience "Salt Lake County property managers"' and 'approve offer "free walkthrough"' with --approver and --reference exit 0 and store scope 'audience' and 'offer' with that text as item and lead_id NULL; with '--lead 1' the activity has lead_id 1.

Each of these exits 1, prints one stderr line starting with the given prefix, and appends no activity: blank --reference ('error: reference:'); blank --approver ('error: approver:'); 'approve lead 99' with no lead 99 and 'approve lead abc' ('error: lead:'); 'approve draft' without --lead ('error: lead:'); 'approve draft' naming a missing file ('error: draft:'); a blank audience or offer item ('error: item:'); '--date 2026-12-01' and '--date 30/11/2026' ('error: date:'); 'approve offer x --lead 99' ('error: lead:'). 'approve vendor x ...' exits 2.
uv run pytest, uv run ruff check ., uv run mypy . and uv run ruff format --check . all pass.

tasks.title: claims file and claim approvals: a claim is verified only when the file and a founder claim approval agree
tasks.goal: Ship config/claims.yaml with the five R-19 claims unverified, a loader that refuses malformed claims, 'approve claim ID' that records the approval and a claim_verified activity, and 'cottonwood claims' that prints each claim's effective status and names every mismatch between the file and the recorded approvals (R-19).
tasks.plan:
1. cottonwood/claims.py: STATUSES ('verified','unverified','prohibited'); Claim frozen dataclass; ClaimsError(location, message) with str 'PATH: LOCATION: MESSAGE'; DEFAULT_CLAIMS_PATH = Path('config/claims.yaml'); load_claims(path) with yaml.safe_load, a top-level 'claims' list, and per claim: id lower-kebab-case and unique, text and evidence non-blank, status in STATUSES, verified needs verified_by non-blank and verified_at a YYYY-MM-DD date, unverified/prohibited need both null; standing_verification(conn, claim_id) -> the latest claim_verified activity whose payload claim_id matches and that no correction voids (events._voided_sql), or None; ClaimStatus(id, status, note); effective_statuses(conn, claims) per spec AC-2.4/2.5.
2. config/claims.yaml with the five claims (fashion-place-attribution, service-area, license-classification, insurance-bonding, prior-company-experience), all unverified, evidence naming the open question in docs/cottonwood-growth-engine.md, verified_by/verified_at null, and a header comment on how a claim becomes verified.
3. cottonwood/gate.py: approve scope 'claim' loads the claims file (claims_path argument), refuses ('claim') an unknown id, a prohibited claim, or one with a standing verification, and appends approval and claim_verified in one transaction; the claim line tells the developer what to put in the file.
4. cottonwood/cli.py: approve gains --claims PATH (default claims.DEFAULT_CLAIMS_PATH); new 'claims' Command with --claims and --db that prints 'ID: STATUS' or 'ID: STATUS (NOTE)' per claim and exits 1 on any note; a ClaimsError prints 'error: ...' and exits 1.
5. tests/test_claims.py: shipped file content, every loader refusal, approve claim payloads and refusals, effective statuses for agreeing, verified-without-approval, approved-but-unverified and voided cases.
acceptance_criteria: config/claims.yaml loads with claims.load_claims and lists exactly five claims with ids fashion-place-attribution, service-area, license-classification, insurance-bonding and prior-company-experience, each with non-empty text, status 'unverified', non-empty evidence, and verified_by and verified_at null.

'cottonwood claims --claims FILE' exits 1 and prints a stderr line starting 'error:' that names FILE, the claim (its index or id) and the field, for each of these files: a claim with no id; two claims with the same id; an id 'Service_Area'; blank text; blank evidence; status 'maybe'; a verified claim with no verified_by; a verified claim with verified_at '30/11/2026'; an unverified claim with verified_by set; a prohibited claim with verified_at set.

With utc_now pinned to 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z, 'cottonwood approve claim service-area --approver Founder --reference "email 2026-11-30 Re: claims" --claims FILE' exits 0, prints 'approval N recorded: claim service-area by Founder; mark it verified in config/claims.yaml with verified_by: Founder and verified_at: 2026-11-30', and appends an 'approval' activity (scope 'claim', item 'service-area') and a 'claim_verified' activity whose payload has claim_id 'service-area', approval_activity_id equal to the approval's id, verified_by 'Founder' and verified_at '2026-11-30'. 'approve claim' exits 1 with a stderr line starting 'error: claim:' and appends nothing for an id not in FILE, for a prohibited claim, and for a claim that already has a claim_verified activity no correction voids.

'cottonwood claims --claims FILE' prints one line per claim in file order, 'ID: STATUS', and exits 0 when they agree: a claim marked verified with verified_by Founder and verified_at 2026-11-30 and a matching claim_verified activity prints 'ID: verified'; a prohibited claim prints 'ID: prohibited'; an unverified claim with no approval prints 'ID: unverified'.

'cottonwood claims --claims FILE' exits 1 when a claim is marked verified with no matching unvoided claim_verified activity (also when verified_by or verified_at differ, or the activity is voided by a correction), printing 'ID: unverified (marked verified but no matching claim approval)', and when a claim has a claim_verified activity but the file says unverified, printing 'ID: unverified (approved on 2026-11-30 by Founder; mark it verified in the claims file)'. Without --claims it reads config/claims.yaml.
uv run pytest, uv run ruff check ., uv run mypy . and uv run ruff format --check . all pass.

tasks.title: suppress command: add a normalized address to suppression without a lead
tasks.goal: Let the developer suppress an email address that belongs to no lead, normalized like every suppression check, leaving an existing entry unchanged, so an opt-out from any channel is honored by import, set-eligibility and the send gate (R-24).
tasks.plan:
1. cottonwood/gate.py: SUPPRESS_SOURCE = 'suppress'; SuppressResult(email_norm, added, added_at, reason) with line() ('suppressed EMAIL' or 'EMAIL already suppressed since DENVER_DATE (REASON)'); suppress(conn, email, reason, source, now): normalize.normalize_email, refuse ('email') blank or not exactly one '@' with text on both sides, refuse ('reason') blank reason, then in BEGIN IMMEDIATE read the existing row (report it unchanged) or insert (email_norm, reason, source or SUPPRESS_SOURCE, now).
2. cottonwood/cli.py: suppress Command with positional email, --reason (required), --source, --db.
3. tests/test_suppress.py with utc_now pinned: stored row, --source, already-suppressed line and unchanged row, refusals, and that prospects-import then imports the contact ineligible and set-eligibility refuses eligible.
acceptance_criteria: With utc_now pinned to 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z, 'cottonwood suppress " Alice@Example.COM " --reason "asked by phone"' exits 0, prints 'suppressed alice@example.com', and stores one suppression row with email_norm 'alice@example.com', reason 'asked by phone', source 'suppress' and added_at '2026-12-01T00:00:00Z'; with '--source "phone call"' the row's source is 'phone call'.

Running 'cottonwood suppress alice@example.com --reason other' when alice@example.com was suppressed at 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z with reason 'asked by phone' exits 0, prints 'alice@example.com already suppressed since 2026-11-30 (asked by phone)', and leaves the suppression row's reason, source and added_at unchanged.

'suppress alice@example.com --reason "  "' prints a stderr line starting 'error: reason:', and each of '  ', 'alice', 'a@b@c', '@example.com' and 'alice@' as the address prints a stderr line starting 'error: email:'; each exits 1 and stores no suppression row.

After 'cottonwood suppress alice@example.com --reason x', 'prospects-import' of a valid direct_candidate record whose contact email is 'ALICE@example.com' imports that contact with eligibility 'ineligible', and 'set-eligibility' of that contact to eligible exits 1.
uv run pytest, uv run ruff check ., uv run mypy . and uv run ruff format --check . all pass.
